kept.title: Skill-load gate works as claimed, but has no unit test
kept.detail: I called preEdit on a throwaway workspace. A Rust edit was denied before `temper:rust-craft` was loaded. After a PostToolUse Skill event, a clean edit was allowed and an `unwrap` was still denied. The subagents (`skills:` preload via PRELOADED) bypass it correctly. The implementation is at hooks.mjs ~L249 and postTool L519. However, no file in tests/ exercises postTool, skillLoaded or the deny-skill-gate path. hooks.test.mjs only notes that the skill gate 'is not under test here' (L76). The behaviour is covered by the single manual smoke run only.

kept.verifier_notes: The claim holds up. tests/hooks.test.mjs:76 has the comment "A preloaded agent type skips the skill gate, which is not under test here." Every test input uses agent_type 'temper:rust-implementer', which matches PRELOADED, so the deny-skill-gate branch at hooks.mjs:255-259 never runs in unit tests. Searching tests/ for skillLoaded, postTool, PostToolUse, skill-gate, skillGate, deny-skill and skill-loaded finds nothing apart from that comment. The only other reference to the skill is the Skill entry in smoke.sh's --allowedTools list, which asserts nothing about the gate. postTool is at hooks.mjs:519 and the gate at 255, as cited. kept.title: The review verdict and gate state can be forged through Bash, so independence is trust-based
kept.plan_ref: README.md layer 6 'Yes (heuristic for shell)' and layer 8
kept.detail: Write and Edit to `.git/` and the temper state dir are denied (hooks.mjs L233). preBash has no equivalent rule. I confirmed that `echo x > .git/temper/verdicts/abc.json`, `cp ... .git/temper/verdicts/a.json` and a python `open(...,'w')` against that path all return allow. Verdicts and the gate cache are plain JSON keyed by fingerprint, and `temper status` prints the fingerprint. So a determined or confused agent could write an 'approved' verdict and a green gate record, defeating the review requirement. The README labels shell checks heuristic but does not say that review state is writable from the shell. This is a hardening gap, not a failure of the intended case of a lazy but honest agent. It matters if the plugin is pitched as a hard gate for client work. A deny rule for shell writes to `.git/temper` is cheap, and the CI gate would still catch real violations.
evidence: chk.mjs against preBash: '.git/temper/verdicts' redirect, cp and python open => allow
scripts/lib/hooks.mjs:233 (Write/Edit denied under .git) versus :429-490 (no .git/temper pattern in SHELL_WRITE_*)
kept.verifier_notes: Evidence holds. hooks.mjs:237-238 denies Write/Edit under the state dir or .git, with a message that names verdicts and gate state. SHELL_WRITE_* (lines 349-353) cover only .rs, Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, temper-baseline.json and the vendored .claude/temper copy; none covers .git/temper. I ran preBash on `echo x > .git/temper/verdicts/abc.json` and on a `cp` into the same directory, and both returned {} (allow). verdict.mjs:76 and :81 store verdicts as plain JSON files keyed by fingerprint in stateDir/verdicts. The README layer 6 row says "Yes (heuristic for shell)". The medium severity is reasonable: the CI gate still backstops it, and the threat model is an agent that acts maliciously or by mistake. I did not run the python open() case, and I did not check whether the gate cache is writable the same way. The verdict forgery claim stands without them.

kept.title: Completion-gate escape valves are not described in the README's 'Done means green and reviewed'
kept.detail: The gate allows a stop after one block when the tree has not changed (the 'loop breaker', hooks.mjs L571-L591), and it is skipped entirely in plan mode or when the final message says `Status: WIP` or `Status: BLOCKED`. The troubleshooting page documents the loop breaker (L120) and the README mentions the WIP and BLOCKED exit. But the layer 7 text says 'Done means green and independently reviewed' without saying the agent can self-declare WIP or hit the second-stop release. So Stop is an honesty-prompt gate, not a hard one. CI and the pre-commit hook are the hard stop. The README should say this plainly.
kept.verifier_notes: The finding is real but overstated. Verified in the clone: the loop breaker (stuck() at hooks.mjs ~L563, the two stop-allowed branches ~L571-L591) exists, plan mode returns none() at L548, and WIP/BLOCKED skips enforcement at L555-L558. The finding itself concedes this. The only real gap is that the second-stop release (loop breaker) and plan-mode skip are not stated in the README. Status stale-doc/low holds, with the narrower scope. The 'honesty-prompt gate, not hard' framing is a fair inference from the code, since CI and pre-commit are the hard stop.

kept.title: Engine state (review verdicts, gate cache) can be forged with a shell write; the Stop hook trusts it

kept.detail: Verdicts are stored at .git/temper/verdicts/<fp>.json and gate results at .git/temper/gate/<fp>.json. preEdit denies Edit/Write under the state dir (hooks.mjs:236-239), but preBash has no rule for it. Probe: `echo '{"verdict":"approved"}' > .git/temper/verdicts/<fp>.json` and `cp /tmp/v.json .git/temper/gate/<fp>.json` both return no decision. completionGate runs runGate, which returns a cached JSON for the fingerprint without re-running anything after fmt (gate.mjs:203-207), and then accepts any cached verdict whose verdict is 'approved' (hooks.mjs:580-581). An agent that writes these two files with the current fingerprint (shown by `temper status`) ends the turn as 'gate green and review approved' with neither having run. CI re-runs the gate, but nothing outside the session re-checks the independent review. This takes deliberate adversarial behaviour, but it defeats the property the README presents as 'Yes, deterministic'. Fix options: deny shell writes whose target matches .git/temper or the state dir in preBash; sign or HMAC state records with a per-session secret kept outside the repo; or re-validate the verdict JSON against verdict.mjs at Stop.

kept.title: Fail-open design: hook errors, malformed input, hook timeouts and the loop breaker all let the action proceed
kept.detail: temper.mjs:59-65 catches any handler exception, prints a systemMessage and exits 0, so the edit, bash command or stop proceeds. Malformed stdin JSON exits 0 with no message (temper.mjs:56; probe: `echo 'not json' | temper hook pre-edit` -> exit 0, no output). The Stop loop breaker lets a turn end with a RED gate or no review after one block if the tree did not change (hooks.mjs:567-574, 583-586). An invalid final reviewer verdict on the second attempt is dropped silently (hooks.mjs:613). These are deliberate choices that keep a session from wedging, and most are documented in troubleshooting.md. The consequence is that the in-session layers are best-effort, and CI is the only fail-closed backstop. The CLI's own gate does fail closed: an unavailable toolchain exits 1 (temper.mjs:94). The silent parse failure is worth a systemMessage, as the exception path already gets.

In scripts/lib/hooks.mjs, the Stop loop breaker (the `stuck()` check) emits only a notice for a red gate or a missing review when the fingerprint is unchanged. The reviewer path with `stop_hook_active` returns `none()` on an invalid verdict. docs/troubleshooting.md lists the loop breaker around line 120. The CLI gate returns exit 1 when `res.ok` is false, which covers an unavailable toolchain. The title also mentions hook timeouts, and I did not check that part. It is a minor overreach in the title. kept.title: Verdict validation accepts degenerate evidence: suffix matching on files_read, and an all-'n/a' approval
kept.plan_ref: README.md:21 layer 8 (verdict validated: unread changed files are refused)
kept.detail: The 'changed files not reviewed' check matches with `r.endsWith(f) || f.endsWith(r)` (verdict.mjs:55-58), so files_read: ["s"] or ["lib.rs"] counts as reading every changed .rs file that ends with that suffix. Every score may be 'n/a', and the >=3 rule only applies to integer scores (verdict.mjs:64). With no cached gate for the fingerprint, the red-gate check is skipped. Probe: an 'approved' verdict with every score 'n/a' and files_read ['s'] against two changed files validates with []. The Stop hook still requires its own green gate, so the exposure is the quality of review evidence, not the gate. Fix: require path-component matches and at least N applicable integer scores.
kept.verifier_notes: I re-opened scripts/lib/verdict.mjs in the clone and the code matches the finding. The changed-files check is `ctx.changedRust.filter((f) => f.endsWith('.rs') && !read.some((r) => r.endsWith(f) || f.endsWith(r)))`. That is a bare suffix match in both directions, so files_read ["s"] satisfies every changed path ending in "s". Scores accept 'n/a' for every dimension, and the "approved requires >=3" rule only inspects `Number.isInteger(scores[d])`, so an all-'n/a' approval is not caught. The red-gate check only runs when `ctx.gate && ctx.gate.ok === false`, so it is skipped when no cached gate exists for the fingerprint. The files_read/commands_run non-empty checks pass with trivial values. I did not re-run the engine-probe; the claim follows directly from the code. The line numbers are approximate but close. Low severity is fair because the Stop hook has its own gate, as the finding says.

The only matches in release.yml were the header comment, workflow_dispatch, the pinned claude-code validate steps, and the `release` environment. kept.title: CI hang or flake: main run 69 red, PR #52 needed a rerun
kept.detail: Main run 69 (PR #51 merge) had both jobs cancelled after about 15 minutes, with no test failure, and PR #52 CI took about 53 minutes wall clock over two attempts. Concurrency cancel-in-progress also cancelled three main runs (50, 55, 56) on back-to-back merges, which can leave main commits unverified. Windows job has timeout 30m and Checks 60m, yet cancellations happened at about 15 minutes, so the cause is unexplained (possibly runner loss). Not investigated or tracked in an issue.
evidence: ci.yml:12-14 concurrency cancel-in-progress true, also applies to main pushes
kept.verifier_notes: The cited evidence matches the claim. evidence-github.md lines 46-48 record run 69 (PR#51 merge) with both jobs cancelled after about 15 minutes (20:09 to 24), and runs 50, 55 and 56 cancelled by concurrency. Run 70 (PR#52) needed attempt 2 and took about 53 minutes (20:43 to 21:36). ci.yml has concurrency cancel-in-progress true at lines 12-14 with no push-only carve-out, timeout-minutes 60 on Checks (line 20) and 30 on Windows (line 48). The "cause unexplained" claim holds: run 69 was cancelled at 20:24, but PR#52's main run came later, so concurrency does not explain it, and a 15-minute cancel is below both job timeouts. The finding's own "not investigated" claim rests only on the evidence file, which I did not check against the issue tracker. The finding calls the 15-minute cancellation a "hang", but the evidence only shows "cancelled", so the cause could be a manual cancel or runner loss. Main was green again at run 71 and run 73 (HEAD d87d887), so the impact is limited. I rate severity low rather than medium.

`temper baseline --check` -> 'cargo metadata --no-deps failed (exit 101): failed to load manifest for workspace member .../crates/*'
kept.verifier_notes: I reproduced the core claim. In an empty workspace with members = ["crates/*"], both `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo metadata --no-deps` fail with "failed to load manifest for workspace member .../crates/*". Its fallback (gate.mjs:58-70) takes the last 15 non-empty lines when nothing matches the FAILED/error patterns, which explains the raw help text. gate2.txt does contain the proper 'failed to load manifest' error, so the message varies by case. refuted.title: Main CI run 69 cancelled after ~15 min and PR #52 needed a rerun: flaky or slow CI
refuted.notes: The facts hold up but the diagnosis and remedy do not. Run 69 (43d70d5, PR#51 merge) did end in failure after about 15 minutes (20:09:28 to 20:24:53), and PR#52's run needed a second attempt. However, ci.yml already sets timeout-minutes: 60 on the Checks job (line 20) and 30 on the second job (line 48), so the recommended "timeout-minutes cap" already exists. ci.yml also has concurrency group ci-${{ github.ref }} with cancel-in-progress: true (lines 12-14). Main pushes sharing a ref cancel each other. The evidence file itself says runs 56, 55 and 50 were cancelled this way. A cancellation at about 15 minutes, with a later main push (the PR#52 merge, run 71) following, is consistent with concurrency cancellation, not a hang. A 15-minute cancel is also far below the 30 and 60 minute timeouts. I did not find evidence of a hang or a flaky test. The 53-minute PR#52 attempt is a slow-runner or queue observation with no root cause shown. The finding presents a hang as the likely cause and proposes an already-present fix, so it is mis-diagnosed. If kept at all, it should be reworded as "main run cancelled by concurrency; PR#52 run slow on a rerun". Even then, severity is informational, not a risk.

refuted.title: Version tags missing from the audit clone; 1.2.3 simulated from commit a485408
refuted.notes: The literal observations reproduce: git tag returns 0 in the clone, and the plugin.json log shows 2495d0e (1.3.0) and a485408 (1.2.3). But the finding is not a defect in the temper project. The clone's origin is the local path /home/user/temper, and git ls-remote --tags on it returned nothing, so the missing tags come from how the audit clone was made, not from the repository. evidence-github.md lines 60-66 show tags v1.0.0 through v1.3.0 exist upstream, and v1.3.0 was tagged by the Release workflow run on 2026-10-05. AGENTS.md already says release-check needs `git fetch --tags`. The finding itself calls this "most likely a clone or fetch artifact". Filing it as a "risk" against the project gap-fresh-adopter-experience is misleading, because it is an audit-process limitation with no adopter impact. At most it belongs in the audit's methodology caveats.
